mainTopic: Using a father's or one's own set-aside חטאת funds for a different sin, and when a husband can no longer cancel his wife's נזירות
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a חטאת. The word ״קרבנו״ teaches that a son cannot use money his father set aside for a חטאת. ״קרבנו על חטאתו״ teaches that even a person's own offering must be for the specific sin it was set aside for. The ברייתא explains that an animal set aside for חלב cannot be brought for דם, since such an animal brings no מעילה and no כפרה. It then considers that money might be switchable, because switched money does bring מעילה and כפרה, but ״על חטאתו״ rules that out too. רבא tries to use the ברייתא's word ״בהמה״ against רב נחמן's view that a blemished animal is like unallocated money. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means an unblemished animal, and that a blemished animal is only good for its value, which is just money. A new משנה then teaches when a husband can no longer cancel his wife's נזירות: after זריקת הדם, or after שחיטה according to רבי עקיבא. The משנה adds the distinction between תגלחת הטהרה and תגלחת הטומאה and brings רבי מאיר's dissent. The גמרא begins by noting that the משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר, who holds that shaving is required.

steps.title: His own offering, not his father's
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes a mistaken line of thought and uses the word ״קרבנו״ to show that a son cannot use his father's sin-offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One might have thought he can use his father's money,] since that applies when the coins are unallocated and not when they are allocated. So the verse says: "His offering." He fulfills his duty with his own offering, but not with his father's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes an idea that started before this section: maybe a son can use money his father set aside for a חטאת. Then it brings a פסוק to reject that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea compared the father's money to money that is still unallocated. The word ״קרבנו״, "his offering," shows that the offering must belong to the person who sinned. So the father's offering does not work for the son.

keyTerms.meaning: Unallocated; money set aside without saying which offering it is for
Allocated; money clearly set aside for a specific offering
The verse teaches; introduces a פסוק that settles the question

steps.title: His own offering must be for his specific sin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that a person may move his own offering from one sin to another. It rejects this with ״קרבנו על חטאתו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: he cannot use the money his father set aside, even from a lighter sin to a lighter sin, or from a severe sin to a severe sin. But he can use an offering he set aside for himself, even from a lighter sin to a severe one, or from a severe sin to a lighter one. So the verse says: "his offering ... for his sin." His offering must be for the sake of his particular sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new idea: maybe a person's own offering is flexible and can be used for any of his sins. Then it uses a פסוק to reject that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion was that only the father's money is a problem, while his own animal can be switched freely between lighter and more severe sins. The words ״על חטאתו״, "for his sin," show that the offering must be set aside for the exact sin it atones for. So switching does not work, even with his own offering.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought; introduces an idea that will be rejected
Set aside, designated
A lighter, less severe sin
A more severe sin
For the sake of his specific sin

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this step is still only about the father's money. The new point is about the person's OWN offering: even that cannot be moved to a different sin.

steps.title: Maybe his own animal can never be switched at all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a stricter possibility: an animal a person set aside for himself cannot be used for any other sin, even one of the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might have thought that he does not fulfill his obligation with an animal he set aside for himself, whether from a lighter sin for a lighter sin or from a severe sin for a severe sin, and certainly not from a lighter sin for a severe one or from a severe sin for a lighter one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proposes a new, stricter idea that it will need to deal with. This line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step showed that an offering must be for its own sin. Now the ברייתא considers going further: maybe even switching between sins of the same level is not allowed, and certainly not between different levels. The reason for this idea comes in the next step.

steps.title: The proof from חלב and דם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports the strict idea with a known rule: an animal set aside for eating חלב and brought for eating דם brings no מעילה and no כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if he set aside an animal for eating forbidden fat and brought it for eating blood, or set it aside for blood and brought it for fat, he has not committed מעילה and he has not gained atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason behind the strict idea from step 3. It points to a case where moving an animal from one sin to another simply does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב and דם are two different sins that each require a חטאת. If the animal is moved from one to the other, he has not committed מעילה, and he also gets no כפרה. This shows that an animal stays tied to its original sin. The ברייתא never rejects this point about an animal; it uses it as a contrast to the case of money in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat; eating it by mistake requires a חטאת

Committed מעילה, misuse of consecrated property

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת is tied to its specific sin. The ברייתא even considers that no switching is allowed at all, because an animal set aside for חלב and brought for דם gives no כפרה.

steps.title: Maybe money can be switched between sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that money set aside for one sin might be usable for any other sin, light or severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps a person can use money he set aside for himself to switch from one sin to another: light to light, severe to severe, severe to light, or light to severe.
steps.whatsHappening: After saying an animal cannot be switched, the ברייתא now raises a new possibility: maybe money is different and can be switched. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ruling out switching an animal, the ברייתא considers that money might be different and could be moved freely between sins in all four directions. Its reason for this idea comes in the next step, and step 7 rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (coins)
Set aside, designated
A lighter sin

steps.title: Support: switched money brings מעילה and still brings כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports the idea that money can be switched, citing the rule that such money brings both מעילה and כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if he set aside money for a sin-offering for eating חלב and brought it for eating דם, or for דם and brought it for חלב, he has committed מעילה and still gained כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a reason to back up the idea that money can be switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an animal (step 4), switching brought no מעילה and no כפרה. With money, the ברייתא notes the opposite: there is מעילה and there is כפרה. So it seems money really can be moved to another sin.

steps.title: The פסוק ״על חטאתו״ rules out switching money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the suggestion: the פסוק requires that the offering be for the specific sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says ״על חטאתו״, for his sin: the offering must be brought for the sake of his own sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shuts down the idea that money can be switched, using a word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though money has some flexibility, ״על חטאתו״ teaches that a חטאת must be brought for the exact sin it was meant for. So money set aside for one sin cannot be used for another, and the ברייתא ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק comes to teach
His sin
For the sake of his specific sin

steps.whatToRemember: ״קרבנו על חטאתו״: a חטאת must belong to the person and be for his specific sin. This holds even for money set aside, not just for an animal.

phrases.english: The verse states: “For his sin”

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that money can be switched between sins
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק requires the offering to be for the specific sin it was set aside for

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא says 'animal,' so it should include a blemished one
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the ברייתא speaks of an animal without limits, suggesting even a blemished animal cannot be used by the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches about an animal. Doesn't that mean even a blemished animal?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא is finished, רבא uses it to challenge רב נחמן, who held that a blemished animal is like general money the son may use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a son cannot bring his father's animal and made no exception. If that includes a blemished animal, then a blemished animal is treated as set aside for a specific offering. That goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches
Doesn't it mean...?
A blemished animal, unfit for an offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The whole long ברייתא was quoted so רבא could use its word ״בהמה״ against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches 'an animal,'
is it not even a blemished one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the finished ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a blemished animal is like general money the son may use
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's unlimited word ״בהמה״ seems to include a blemished animal, so the son could not use it.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means an unblemished animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading: the ברייתא speaks only of an unblemished animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means an unblemished animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא by limiting the ברייתא's word ״בהמה״ to an unblemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an animal fit for the altar counts as set aside for a specific offering. A blemished animal can still be like general money, so רב נחמן's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An unblemished animal, fit for an offering

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's ban on a son using his father's animal applies to an unblemished animal. רב נחמן's view about a blemished animal survives.

phrases.english: No, an unblemished one.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's reading that ״בהמה״ includes a blemished animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as referring only to an unblemished animal

steps.title: Why not teach the case of a blemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a blemished animal is treated like unallocated money. If it is, why did the ברייתא pick money as its example instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a blemished animal? Is it like unallocated money? If so, why does the ברייתא specifically speak of money his father set aside? It should teach the case of a blemished animal!
steps.whatsHappening: After step 9 limited the ברייתא to an unblemished animal, the גמרא now asks about a blemished one. If it counts like unallocated money, why didn't the ברייתא simply use it as the example?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the ברייתא's ban on the son using the animal covers only an unblemished animal. That suggests a blemished animal may be used like סתומה money. If so, the ברייתא's choice of מעות seems strange, since a blemished animal would have been a fine example too.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemished animal, unfit to be brought on the מזבח
Unallocated, meaning money set aside without saying which offering it is for
Why specifically this case? It challenges the choice of example
Let it teach, meaning it should have said

phrases.english: But a blemished animal, what is its law?
Is it like an unallocated one?
phrases.notes: He means like the unallocated money from the ברייתא, which the son may use for his own offerings.

phrases.english: Why specifically does it teach
money that his father set aside?
Let it teach a blemished animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the reading in step 9 by asking about the blemished animal. Step 11 answers this.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice of 'money his father set aside' as its example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a blemished animal works like unallocated money, the ברייתא could have used it as its example. Choosing money instead suggests the two are not the same.

steps.title: A blemished animal is really just money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a blemished animal is indeed like money. It is only good for its value, so teaching money already covers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed so. For what is a blemished animal fit? Only for its value, and value is money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that a blemished animal is like unallocated money. It explains that the ברייתא did not need to mention it separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח, so its only use is to be sold for its value. Since its value is simply money, the case of מעות already includes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed so, accepting the point raised
Is fit for, or is usable for
Its value or price

steps.whatToRemember: A blemished sacrificial animal is treated like its money value, so the rule about unallocated money also applies to it.

phrases.english: Indeed so,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and explains the wording

steps.title: When the husband can no longer cancel his wife's נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that once the blood of one of the נזירה's offerings is sprinkled, her husband cannot cancel her vow. רבי עקיבא says this applies even once one animal is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the blood of one of her offerings was sprinkled on her behalf, he cannot cancel her vow. רבי עקיבא says: even if just one of the animals was slaughtered on her behalf, he cannot cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the point at the end of a woman's נזירות after which her husband can no longer cancel the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sets the cutoff at זריקת הדם of any one of her offerings. רבי עקיבא sets an earlier cutoff: as soon as any one of the animals is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sprinkled, here the blood thrown on the מזבח
To cancel a vow, which a husband may do for his wife
Was slaughtered

phrases.english: MISHNA: If there was sprinkled on her behalf
the blood of one of the offerings,
he cannot cancel her vow.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Even if there was slaughtered on her behalf
one of all the animals,
he cannot cancel her vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ נזרק עליה אחד מן הדמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once blood is sprinkled, or according to רבי עקיבא once an animal is slaughtered, the husband can no longer cancel her נזירות.

steps.title: The rule applies only to the purity shaving
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the rule to תגלחת הטהרה. At a תגלחת הטומאה the husband can still cancel, because she would have to restart and he does not want a wife who is held back. רבי מאיר says he can cancel even at תגלחת הטהרה, because he does not want a shaven wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? At the shaving of purity. But at the shaving of impurity he may cancel, because he can say: I do not want a wife who is held back. רבי מאיר says: even at the shaving of purity he may cancel, because he can say: I do not want a shaven wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains when its rule applies. It then brings רבי מאיר, who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After תגלחת הטומאה, the נזירה must start her נזירות over, so she will keep holding back from wine. That is a real hardship for the husband, which gives him the right to cancel. רבי מאיר adds that the shaving itself also affects him, so he can cancel even at the purity shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? It introduces a limit on the rule
The shaving at the normal, pure end of נזירות
The shaving after a נזיר became impure, after which the נזירות restarts
Held back or downcast, here a wife who cannot drink wine
I do not want

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'he can say I do not want...' is not about the wife's vow being bad in general. It is the husband's legal reason that the vow affects him personally, and that is what lets him cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 12 and adds a dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cutoff applies only at תגלחת הטהרה. At תגלחת הטומאה the husband can cancel, and רבי מאיר lets him cancel at both.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר. He holds that shaving is required to end the נזירות, so before she shaves she is still forbidden to drink wine, and the husband could still cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר. For רבי אליעזר said that shaving is necessary. Since she has not shaved, she is still forbidden to drink wine. And since she is held back, he can cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining which תנא the משנה cannot match. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, the נזירות does not end until the shaving, even after the blood is sprinkled. So after זריקה she is still banned from wine, which is the very hardship that lets a husband cancel. That contradicts the משנה's rule that he cannot cancel after זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is required, meaning the נזירות does not end without it
Wine
Being held back or downcast
He is able to cancel

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the husband's right to cancel to whether the נזירות is still in force, which depends on the dispute about whether shaving is required.

And since she is held back,
